scan company_type/kind.{offsets,data}.bin for exact match, read company_type/id.bin[r]

dimension_resolution.method: single scan over 234,997 rows; for surviving rows set both bitset_by_rowpos and a uint8_t allowed_by_id[max_company_id+1] flag for O(1) lookup from mc.company_id

join_order.notes: Driver. Each row gives a movie_id. Dedup is not required because subsequent join semantics already allow duplicates; collect into vector<int32_t> candidate_movie_ids and dedup with sort+unique for efficiency.

join_order.probe: for each candidate_movie_id v, fetch title row via indexes/title__id__pos.bin; check 1950 <= production_year <= 2010
primary CSR movie_info__movie_id for v -> scan movie_info/info varlen; test against unordered_set of 9 literals
join_order.notes: Hash set built once over 9 literals at query start. Short-circuit on first hit per movie.

join_order.notes: For surviving mc rows we still need company_name.name for MIN aggregate -> use company_name__id__pos to map mc.company_id -> cn rowpos -> read cn/name varlen.

data_structures.candidate_movie_ids: std::vector<int32_t> sorted+unique from movie_link aux CSR
data_structures.company_name_allowed_by_id: std::vector<uint8_t>(max_company_id+1) flag array — 0/1 membership for O(1) test from mc.company_id
data_structures.running_mins: three std::string locals (min_cn_name, min_lt_link, min_title); init to sentinel high; lex-min update

parallelism.rationale: Driver set is small (~2-6k candidate movies after movie_link aux probe). Per-movie work is a handful of small CSR probes. Parallel overhead would exceed the work. Use single thread to avoid mutex contention on the three running min strings.

indexes.purpose: movie_id -> title rowpos for production_year + title varlen
movie_id -> mi row range for IN-list semi-join
movie_id -> mk row range for keyword semi-join
movie_id -> mc row range for note/company_type_id/company_id filters
mc.company_id -> cn rowpos to read cn.name for MIN
ml.link_type_id -> lt rowpos to read lt.link for MIN (within link_type_ids set)

execution_notes: Order of per-candidate semi-join probes: cheapest+most-selective first. Recommended per-movie order: (a) production_year range (single int compare via title__id__pos), (b) movie_keyword sequel check (typically <=10 mk rows per title), (c) movie_info IN-list (avg ~6 mi rows per title), (d) movie_companies full check (which also yields company_name + link_type lookups for MIN).

For MIN aggregates we cannot early-exit per movie because a later movie may produce a lex-smaller string. However within a single movie's mc rows, after the first valid (movie, mc, ml) combination we still must enumerate ALL ml rows of this movie (filtered by link_type_ids) and ALL valid mc rows to update all three mins.

ml-side MIN(lt.link): for each candidate movie that passes everything else, enumerate movie_link rows (primary CSR movie_link__movie_id[v]) whose link_type_id is in link_type_ids; for each, look up lt.link via link_type__id__pos and update min.
Avoid hardcoding any dimension id constant — resolve at runtime per Dimension Literal Resolution section.
All column files mmap'd read-only at startup.
